fixed: Retried the SEC URL per brief (HEAD and GET with browser-like User-Agent, plus web fetcher): all return HTTP 403 with SEC's 'Undeclared Automated Tool' block page - an anti-bot policy block of automated fetchers, not a dead link.

Verified the cited filing is live via SEC's official submissions API (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001622536.json): accession 0001622536-26-000036 = Talen Energy Corp Q1 2026 Form 10-Q, filed 2026-05-05, primary document tln-20260331.htm - exact match to the cited URL.

data.json: kept the canonical SEC URL in actions[5].source_url and sources.urls (no replacement - it is the correct official source; no lower-quality mirror substituted); enriched actions[5].details with the API-confirmed filing metadata (Q1 2026 Form 10-Q, accession 0001622536-26-000036, filed 2026-05-05) for traceability.

NOTES.md: appended a dated 2026-08-11 caveat bullet to the refresh section documenting the 403 (anti-bot, not dead), the official-API verification with source URL, the URL-kept decision, and corroboration of the April-2026 PPA-transition timing by Talen's already-cited 2025-06-11 IR release (spring 2026 front-of-the-meter transition).
remaining_risks: SEC blocks automated content retrieval from www.sec.gov paths (403) in this review environment, so the 10-Q's exact sentence on the April 2026 PPA transition was not re-fetched this pass; the claim rests on the original 2026-08-11 refresh record, whose filing metadata (accession, form, date, primary document) was independently confirmed via SEC's official API.
The data.sec.gov submissions JSON is a bulk filing index (430 filings) - referenced as a verification pointer in the NOTES.md caveat note only, not added to sources.urls.
Reviewer inventory stores this issue string truncated mid-word ('SEC anti-bot bl'); treated as the full single issue for this center.
summary: The single issue for this center was a source spot-check caveat: the Talen Q1 2026 10-Q SEC URL returns HTTP 403. Retry confirmed SEC's anti-bot 'Undeclared Automated Tool' block (not a dead link), and SEC's official submissions API confirmed the filing (accession 0001622536-26-000036, 10-Q filed 2026-05-05) exists exactly as cited, so the URL was kept as canonical. The caveat and verification were documented in NOTES.md and actions[5].details was enriched with the API-confirmed filing metadata; data.json remains valid JSON.
